explanation.value: Fancy numbers with k base-4 digits correspond to k-bit binary masks, so fancy numbers below 4^k number 2^k (counting zero). Read n's base-4 digits from the most significant. At a position with r digits to its right: if n's digit is 0, a fancy number matching so far must also put 0 there; if it is 1, every fancy number that puts 0 there and anything in the lower r digits is smaller, adding 2^r, and we continue matching with 1; if it is 2 or 3, both 0 and 1 are allowed there with any lower digits, adding 2^(r+1), and no fancy number can match this digit, so we stop. The total counts fancy numbers in [0, n), including 0, so subtract 1.
